newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia exchange chief slams Japanese stockbroker.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia exchange chief slams Japanese stockbroker.

text.p: The president of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, in a report published on Monday, slammed a Japanese stockbroker for not giving "accurate news" about the Malaysian market on a popular private television channel.
Salleh Abdul Majid, expressing personal views in a weekly column in the daily Business Times, also lashed out at the TV3 station for presenting "inaccurate" market views "too often".

Salleh said Katsuhiko Abe, managing director of Japan's Yamaichi Advisory Services in Kuala Lumpur, painted "a very gloomy and negative picture" of the market in the TV3 news programme on Friday night. Yamaichi Advisory Services is an affiliate of Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.
Abe had said the market was hit by uncertainty following news that Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad was going on two-months leave, raising questions about the premier's health.
Mahathir, responding to the ruffle in the market, said the long vacation had nothing to do with his health. He will depart next week for a work-and-rest mission.
Salleh criticised Abe for questioning whether Malaysia's decade-long high economic growth rate could be sustained.
"In short, he painted a very gloomy and negative picture of the market.
"Imagine -- all these negative views were presented by the television station as the position the market will hold currently and in the near future," Salleh said.

"The word is 'accurate' or 'non-speculative' as we are trying very hard to stamp out excessive speculation in our market," Salleh wrote. "The views expressed on the market must be well-rounded, and based in facts, not speculation."
Abe said his comments on Mahathir reflected investor concerns when they heard about the premier's vacation plans.
"It's not only me, but everybody...I didn't say it to push down the market," Abe told Reuters.
He said he had received many calls from Japanese clients on the Mahathir news.
Abe also said he was reflecting investor concerns over Malaysia's strong growth, but said he was bullish because the market had dropped in the last one month.
The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange's Composite Index fell 12 percent from March 31 to a low of 1,056.30 points on April 29. The index was at 1,098.10 at midday on Monday.
Salleh also took a swipe at TV3, saying the broadcaster should not only air good news it must report "accurate" and "non-speculative" news.
The station, operated by Sistem Televisyen Malaysia Bhd Bhd, airs comments by financial analysts in a nightly news programme.
TV3 officials were not immediately available for comment.
